children: Shares in Japanese data centre operator Datasection
fell by their daily limit of 150 yen, or more than 18%, on Thursday, amid concerns about the growth potential of the sector that powers AI.
Since the beginning of November, Datasection shares have fallen 65%.
The midterm election results in the US showed that many American voters were concerned about the aggressive buildout of AI data centres, which sent lower the shares of major Asian chip makers.

Datasection shares were also pressured after the company on Monday slashed its sales forecast for the year that ends in March 2027 by nearly 90%, citing the cancellation of an AI infrastructure order.
The company now expects a loss of 1.48 billion yen ($9.27 million) for the current business year, compared with the previous forecast of an 8.7 billion yen profit.

Datasection did not immediately respond to a Reuters query asking about the identity of the company that initially placed the order and if the cancellation was triggered by the tighter control on access to AI chips from the US.
Washington this week unveiled rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips through overseas data centres.

Tencent did not immediately reply to a Reuters query asking if it placed then cancelled the AI infrastructure order with Datasection.
On Wednesday, Tencent said new US restrictions on remote access to advanced AI chips would not substantially hurt its cloud revenue, though they would likely slow development of its next AI model.
